MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  MARCH 20, 2023

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 7:02 p.m. at City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chambers,
  4045 Palos Verdes Dr. N., Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR BAIN.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR BAIN led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Pope, Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina and
  Retz

  Commissioners Absent:  None

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  4.  PRESENTATION

  A.  SOUTH COAST BOTANIC GARDENS ACTIVITY UPDATE

  Stephanie Yinger, Community Relations Manager of the South Coast Botanic
  Gardens, spoke about a new exhibition utilizing trash from the ocean to make art
  called “Washed Ashore” at the Gardens. She noted that the Tropical Butterfly
  Exhibit returns May 1st and their music event “Sunset Series” will begin near
  Memorial Day and go on until Labor Day on Thursday nights.

  Ms. Yinger noted that she does outreach to local schools to inform them of the
  activities available for children at the Gardens, in response to CHAIR BAIN.

  5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF
  FEBRUARY 21, 2023

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
March 20, 2023
   COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ
  to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  FEBRUARY 21, 2023.

  There being no objection, CHAIR BAIN so ordered.

  6.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  **ITEM 7G. TAKEN OUT OF ORDER**

  G.  PORTUGUESE BEND HORSE SHOW REQUEST FOR ARENA #2 RENOVATION

  Assistant City Manager Davis (ACM Davis) provided a staff report (as per the
  agenda material).

  Carole Rowe, Chairperson for the Portuguese Bend Horse Show, presented a
  proposal and the reasoning behind the renovation of the footing for Arena #2. She
  noted that riders shared they felt the current footing was not satisfactory for the
  purposes of showing. She also noted that they lost around 100 riders from last
  year’s event, and many were from some local barns including Seahorse.

  ACM Davis clarified the fiscal impact of the renovation referring to staff report.

  ACM Davis stated that the anticipated renovation time of the project would be
  approximately 14 days for the renovation and an additional five days for settling.
  She also noted that the greater community would benefit from the renovation and
  that the new blended footing would be acceptable for all riders including the jumpers
  in question, as well as western riders, in response to COMMISSIONER RETZ.

  Ms. Rowe stated that they will have the funds collected prior to the renovation and
  have created a strategic planning committee to assist with the fundraising to collect
  the funds needed to cost share for the project, in response to CHAIR BAIN.

  CHAIR BAIN stated that it has become very difficult for non-profit organizations to
  raise this amount of funding. Ms. Rowe noted that they have some early pledges
  and that some funds typically donated to the show may be pledged towards this
  project.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
March 20, 2023
   Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted that this item was brought to the
  Equestrian Committee and the Committee agreed that this was a project that
  needed to be completed.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA, as the representative to the Equestrian Committee,
  stated that the Committee noted the arena is losing riders due to the footing and
  that for enhanced safety of the horses the renovation should be completed. VICE
  CHAIR MCCORMICK asked to what extent the danger is of the current footing in
  the arena. COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA stated that the footing is very deep and is
  hard for horses to trot and canter in that depth of footing. ACM Davis clarified that
  the arena is not unsafe for regular use and, outside of this request, is not planned
  for renovation. She also noted that this renovation improves the arena to not only
  still allow recreational use but provide better footing for jumping which would be
  used for the PBNHS.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  TO RECOMMEND THE CITY COUNCIL REVIEW AND APPROVE
  PROPOSED RENOVATIONS TO ARENA #2.

  AYES:  Persichina, Pope, Retz, Ciarolla, McCormick and Bain
  ABSENT:  None

  A.  REQUEST FOR PERMANENT RESTROOMS AT PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN
  CENTER

  ACM Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  ACM Davis responded that the City has received several different quotes with the
  highest quote being $276,200 for full-cycle purchase and installation by one
  contractor versus the $172,000, which would have the City purchased the building
  independently and complete the pre/post site work separately, in response to
  COMMISSIONER RETZ.

  ACM Davis stated that the operator of the Peter Weber Equestrian Center (PWEC)
  does not have an obligation to cover large capital costs such as this since it is a
  City facility, in response to CHAIR BAIN.

  CHAIR BAIN noted the expense of some of the items listed in the quote and asked
  if it would be a cost saving method to purchase some of these items individually
  and have maintenance install the items. ACM Davis stated that Staff has not
  investigated the costs but felt it would be best to include these items all in one

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
March 20, 2023
   project. She also noted that Staff would look into the cost of these items further to
  recognize savings, if possible, in response to CHAIR BAIN.

  ACM Davis stated there are funds in the City budget to cover the cost of the project
  within Park Facility Fees, in response to COMMISSIONER RETZ.

  ACM Davis stated that the intent was to have a restroom and office building
  structure built during the initial build of the new barn, but the actual costs exceeded
  the initial budget and as a result the additional work was not completed, in response
  to COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA.

  ACM Davis stated that it does not appear there will be any grants available to offset
  costs of a restroom facility, in response to COMMISSIONER RETZ.

  ACM Davis stated that Staff has presented everything regarding the scope of ADA
  accessibility to Willdan, the City’s Public Works engineer contractor, for review
  regarding ADA accessibility. She also noted that Staff anticipates that by the time
  everything is proposed to the City Council the final scope will be confirmed, in
  response to CHAIR BAIN.

  CHAIR BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  TO RECOMMEND THAT THE CITY COUNCIL REVIEW AND APPROVE A
  NEW RESTROOM STRUCTURE TO BE INSTALLED AT PETER WEBER
  EQUESTRIAN CENTER IN A NOT-TO-EXCEED AMOUNT OF $172,000
  AND FOR STAFF TO TAKE IN ACCOUNT ANY ADDITIONAL COST
  SAVINGS.

  AYES:  Persichina, Pope, Retz, Ciarolla, McCormick and Bain
  ABSENT:  None

  B.  CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECT LIST

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  CHAIR BAIN asked about the priority of execution of the items on the list.
  Community Services Pinuelas stated Staff will present the items to Council to get
  feedback regarding what should be included in the budget as a general priority of
  execution. She also noted items will remain on the Capital Improvement Project List
  even if they are not completed during the next budget cycle. ACM Davis noted that
  the City operates on a two-year budget cycle and that Staff will prioritize based on

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
March 20, 2023
   feedback from the Commission, the Council, and based on what Staff determines
  is manageable to complete during the next two fiscal years.

  ACM Davis stated the City could bring Willdan in to assess engineering estimates
  regarding pathway projects based on decomposed granite or more grading needed
  including the Highridge Park project, in response to CHAIR BAIN.

  CHAIR BAIN requested to add an item to the list regarding tree trimming at
  Highridge Park.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ requested to add an item to the list regarding providing
  some historical signage at Chandler Preserve as well as possible renaming of the
  area due to it being an archaeological site previously being occupied by Native
  Americans.

  ACM Davis stated that due to the last quote received for “Butcher” Park
  development being from a few years ago the estimated cost will likely require
  revision. She also stated it has been shared with the City Council that there may
  need to be a budget adjustment as bids and quotes come in, in response to VICE
  CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  ACM Davis stated that the price of the new fitness equipment associated with the
  Perimeter Pathway project at Ernie Howlett Park was included in the total price that
  was budgeted, in response to COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA.

  ACM Davis stated that there may be a chance to add more fitness equipment to the
  pathway at Ernie Howlett Park in the future if desired. She also stated that Staff is
  planning on installing a map and signage along the pathway to show where the
  equipment is located along the pathway, in response to CHAIR BAIN.

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK requested to look into placing a bench or adding a
  lookout area at the top of George F. Canyon as an additional project. ACM Davis
  stated that she would speak to Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  regarding the request.

  C.  UPDATED SPORTS FIELD POLICY

  Community Services Coordinator Morrow provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that two organizations currently have a contract or
  addendum through the City prior to a policy being established, in response to
  CHAIR BAIN. ACM Davis stated that a main reason for issuing a contract versus
  only a permit is that an organization may have additional facilities or maintenance

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
March 20, 2023
   requirements that the City would require additional upkeep for that would still not
  be stated in a general policy, in response to CHAIR BAIN.

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK suggested adding some additional bullet points to the
  penalties section to help better clarify the section. Supervisor Pinuelas stated Staff
  would look into it and make modifications where needed. ACM Davis noted the
  penalty fee and the possible charge back of Staff fixing an offense is in addition to
  the actual notification of the offense to the organization.

  ACM Davis stated the City has had the need for enforcement but currently Staff is
  only able to communicate to the organization without assessing any penalties. She
  also noted that this is one reason why the sports field policy is being proposed, in
  response to CHAIR BAIN.

  CHAIR BAIN asked whether the City would have the ability to seek out legal means
  if an offense was very egregious and whether this should be stated in the policy.
  ACM Davis stated Staff could work with the City Attorney regarding the proper
  language and add a line to the policy if directed by the Commission.

  ACM Davis stated there are currently no penalty options available to Staff.
  Coordinator Morrow stated that it is listed in the policy that an organization would
  be unable to have a new activity approved without the payment of any penalty fees
  or correction of any infractions, in response to VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked where the Commission stood regarding the Group
  B camp cost section of the policy. She stated that she would agree with Staff’s
  recommendation to suspend the price cap and review the camps when the permit
  was submitted. CHAIR BAIN also agreed that Staff’s recommendation was a good
  solution.

  ACM Davis stated that any new sport camp that is proposed would be brought to
  the Commission. She also stated that Staff would review all camps proposed even
  after they were approved and utilize their discretion on the price of the camp moving
  forward after the initial approval by the Commission, in response to
  COMMISSIONER POPE.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ stated that he was in favor of a price cap but would
  recommend that if not stated in the Policy there be a strong guiding point of a
  standard price as currently listed at $350.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if everyone had reviewed the attached
  sports camp price comparison sheet. The Commissioners affirmed.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
March 20, 2023
   Silver Spur Little League President Al Briese spoke regarding the organization’s
  concerns regarding the Group B sports camps price cap being too low due to
  increasing costs regarding supplies and marketing materials. COMMISSIONER
  PERSICHINA asked Mr. Briese about the costs. He also stated that kids would
  typically provide their own equipment (glove and bat), and that the other equipment
  (pitching nets and hitting machines) are already in place. Mr. Briese agreed but
  stated that the cost of baseballs has risen drastically, and the league does provide
  catcher equipment for the younger age participants.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked Mr. Briese whether the baseballs purchased for the
  camps would be used during the season to which Mr. Briese affirmed. She further
  asked if those costs should be considered as camp cost passed on to the camp
  participants.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that the main goal would be to create affordable
  camps for the kids and to preserve the public nature of the park. Mr. Briese stated
  that he agreed that it is all about the kids and that there are many for-profit camps
  in the area and that all their organization wants to do is offer a camp as a non-profit
  and to have another option available to the residents of the Peninsula.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA stated he feels it is best to keep the camp prices
  low to be able to offer an opportunity for everyone to participate and not price out a
  certain group.

  CHAIR BAIN stated that it did not appear that there was a disagreement with the
  policy keeping the pricing of the camps affordable for public use at the parks. She
  went over the two options available. Supervisor Pinuelas stated Staff could add a
  section that the organization would need to itemize their costs of the camp to justify
  the selected pricing when they submit their application.

  A discussion between the Commission and Staff ensued to clarify the proper way
  to state the motion.

  CHAIR BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to:

  RECOMMEND THAT THE SPORTS FIELD POLICY BE REVISED TO
  INCREASE THE SECOND OFFENSE PENALTY TO $250, ADD
  LANGUAGE FOR A LEGAL ELEMENT FOR ENFORCEMENT, ADD A
  FOURTH BULLET POINT TO THE THIRD PENALTY, AND SET NO
  PRICE CAP BUT A REQUIREMENT TO ITEMIZE COSTS FOR GROUP B
  CAMP COST; AND RECOMMEND THAT THE CITY COUNCIL REVIEW
  AND APPROVE THE SPORTS FIELD USAGE POLICY WITH
  REVISIONS.

  There being no objection, CHAIR BAIN so ordered.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
March 20, 2023
   D.  PROPOSED PARK TOURS SCHEDULE

  Coordinator Morrow provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COMMISSIONER POPE proposed including a tour of the Peter Weber Equestrian
  Center as part of the park tours because of the proposed restrooms project.

  It was suggested to keep the PWEC tour in September and including the tour as
  part of a regular meeting. The Commission agreed with the proposed park tour
  schedule as listed in the report.

  E.  2023 SUMMER CONCERT IN THE PARK PROGRAM

  Coordinator Morrow provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  ACM Davis noted that although it has been great having the PV Symphonic Band
  the previous years, Staff has heard interest from some residents about having a
  more contemporary band. She also noted that there are funds available to support
  estimated costs.

  The Commission and Staff had a brief discussion regarding the two options
  available for this year’s concert. COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded
  by VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  TO ACCEPT STAFF’S RECOMMENDATION TO PROCEED WITH
  OPTION ONE TO USE A PRODUCTION COMPANY WITH A HIRED BAND.

  AYES:  Persichina, Pope, Retz, Ciarolla, McCormick and Bain
  ABSENT:  None

  F.  2023 SUMMER MOVIE NIGHT PROGRAM

  Coordinator Morrow provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  ACM Davis stated that Staff considered a fee for drive-in Movie Nights when those
  were held during the pandemic year, but that would not be the case for this event,
  in response to VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  CHAIR BAIN suggested “The Mitchells vs The Machines” as one of the movies. The
  Commission agreed with that suggestion.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  8
March 20, 2023
   COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA suggested “Toy Story 4” as the other movie. The
  Commission agreed with that suggestion.

  H.  RECREATION FEES REVIEW

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR
  MCCORMICK to:

  APPROVE THE STAFF RECOMMENDATION ON RECREATION FEES
  TO THE CITY COUNCIL.
  There being no objection, CHAIR BAIN so ordered.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  MAYOR’S RIDE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Coordinator Morrow provided a brief update of the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride
  scheduled for Saturday, May 13. He stated that Staff is excited that the local Scouts
  will be back to provide their Pancake Breakfast as in previous years.

  B.  TENNIS CLUB OPEN HOUSE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Coordinator Morrow gave a brief overview of the Tennis Club Open House which
  included a description of the activities, time frame, and marketing of the event.

  C.  19TH AMENDMENT COMMEMORATION PLAQUE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the commemoration of the 100th
  Anniversary of the certification of the 19th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution as
  proposed by Mayor Huff. She noted Staff would work with the Mayor and a working
  group on the plaque design, location, and a dedication ceremony.

  **ITEM 10B TAKEN OUT OF ORDER**

  10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  B.  PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION FUNDRAISING COMMITTEE UPDATE (VERBAL
  REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief update on the Pepper Tree Foundation
  Fundraising Committee and its goals which are to seek funding for large parks
  capital projects, planned giving, and sponsorship of events. She noted that at the

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  9
March 20, 2023
   policy development session, the City Council provided input on a fundraising goal
  and types of fundraising.

  **COMMISSIONER POPE left the meeting at 8:50 pm.**

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  Supervisor Pinuelas noted the current Commissioner recruitment and the deadline
  for applications for the vacant Park and Activities Commission position.

  9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  CHAIR BAIN stated that Highridge Park will need some grading work due to the
  amount of rain the City has received recently.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK suggested the space by George F. Canyon and Taber
  Grove where the water project is being done, and if there was any thought of the
  City doing something at that location. ACM Davis stated Staff would reach out to
  the Public Works Director regarding the plans and report back to the Commission.

  10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTION OF FEBRUARY 28, 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  C.  PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION SISTER CITY REQUEST (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief introduction of an idea proposed by CHAIR BAIN
  and noted that Staff wanted to see if there was any interest from the Commission
  for Staff to proceed further. She stated that CHAIR BAIN would present her idea to
  the Commission.

  CHAIR BAIN presented her idea to share the City’s public spaces with the public in
  surrounding areas. She noted that it is not an intent to partner with a specific city
  as a “Sister City” but for Staff to look into some programming to invite the public
  from surrounding areas that do not have the same amount of public space, to enjoy
  our City’s public spaces. She stated that she wanted to see if there was a

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  10
March 20, 2023
   consensus from the Commission to have Staff look into ideas to bring people from
  other areas to the City’s parks.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ stated that field trips were held at George F Canyon by
  other school districts prior to the pandemic. CHAIR BAIN noted that those events
  were organized by the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy. CHAIR BAIN
  also stated that she would love to see opportunities to have kids see horses and
  run around in the open spaces at the City’s parks as it is an experience that could
  be shared with others.

  The Commission endorsed CHAIR BAIN’s suggestion for Staff to begin exploring
  ideas to present to the Commission later.

  11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  NONE.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR BAIN MOVED TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 9:00 PM TO THE NEXT PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION MEETING ON APRIL 17, 2023, AT 6:00 P.M., WHICH WILL BE
  HELD AT THE CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBER.

  There being no objection, CHAIR BAIN so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  ___________________________
  Matt Morrow  Judy Bain
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  11
March 20, 2023
